text: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Take the whole army with you and go up against Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may take its spoil and its livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."
So Joshua and the whole army set out to go up against Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night,
giving them these orders: "Listen carefully. You are to lie in ambush behind the city. Do not go far from it, and all of you stay ready.
I and all the men with me will approach the city, and when they come out against us as they did before, we will flee from them.
They will pursue us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are running from us as they did before.' So we will flee from them.
Then you will rise up from the ambush and take possession of the city, for the LORD your God will give it into your hand.
When you have captured the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has commanded. See, these are my orders to you."
So Joshua sent them off, and they went to the place of ambush and took up position between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
Early the next morning Joshua mustered the people, and he and the elders of Israel went up ahead of them to Ai.
The whole army that was with him marched up, drew near, and took up position opposite the city. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city.

versions.text: The whole army that was with him marched up, drew near, and came to a halt in front of the city. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city.
versions.explanation: "Came to a halt in front of" is a loose rendering of נֶגֶד הָעִיר ("opposite/facing the city") and reads a little flatly; "took up position opposite the city" is closer and flows better when read aloud.

text: Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
So the forces took their positions—the main camp north of the city and the rear guard west of it—and that night Joshua went out into the middle of the valley.

versions.text: So the forces took their positions—the main camp north of the city and the rear guard west of it—and that night Joshua went down into the valley.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has וַיֵּלֶךְ ... בְּתוֹךְ הָעֵמֶק, "went into the midst of the valley." "Went down into" adds a direction not in the text; "the middle of the valley" preserves בְּתוֹךְ.

text: When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people hurried out early to meet Israel in battle at the appointed place facing the Arabah. But he did not know that an ambush had been set against him behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel let themselves be driven back before them and fled toward the wilderness.
All the men of Ai were summoned to give chase, and as they pursued Joshua they were drawn far from the city.

versions.text: All the men in Ai were called out to pursue them, and as they chased Joshua they were drawn away from the city.
versions.explanation: The verb וַיִּזָּעֲקוּ suggests a rallying cry that mustered the whole population; "were summoned to give chase" captures this more vividly and avoids the double use of "pursue/chase" awkwardness.

text: Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city wide open and pursued Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Stretch out toward Ai the javelin in your hand, for I will give the city into your hand." So Joshua stretched out the javelin in his hand toward the city.
The moment he stretched out his hand, the men in ambush rose quickly from their position and ran. They entered the city, captured it, and set it on fire at once.

When the men of Ai looked back, they saw the smoke of the city rising to the sky, and they had no strength to flee in any direction, for the Israelites who had been fleeing toward the wilderness now turned on their pursuers.
For when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that smoke was rising from it, they turned around and struck down the men of Ai.

The others came out of the city against them, so that the men of Ai were caught in the middle, with Israelites on this side and on that. Israel cut them down, leaving no survivor and none who escaped.
But the king of Ai they took alive and brought to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the open country and in the wilderness where they had chased them, and every one of them had fallen by the sword until none were left, all Israel returned to Ai and put it to the sword.
Twelve thousand fell that day, men and women alike—all the people of Ai.
Joshua did not draw back the hand that held out the javelin until he had devoted to destruction all who lived in Ai.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that city did Israel take for themselves, just as the LORD had commanded Joshua.

versions.text: Only the livestock and the spoil of that city did Israel take for themselves, according to the word the LORD had commanded Joshua.
versions.explanation: "According to the word the LORD had commanded" is awkward English (a word is not commanded); "just as the LORD had commanded Joshua" renders the idiom naturally for oral reading.

text: So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolate place to this day.

He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening, and at sunset Joshua ordered that his body be taken down from the tree and thrown at the entrance of the city gate. Over it they raised a great heap of stones, which is there to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites—an altar of uncut stones, on which no iron tool had been used, as it is written in the Book of the Law of Moses. On it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed fellowship offerings.
There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law that Moses had written.

versions.text: There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law of Moses.
versions.explanation: The relative clause אֲשֶׁר כָּתַב ("which he had written") is dropped from the translation; restoring it preserves the full content of the verse.

versions.text: There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, the law that Moses had written.
versions.explanation: The current wording repeats "Moses" three times in one short clause ("the law of Moses, the law that Moses had written"), which is heavy for oral reading and slightly redundant. Merging the construct phrase with the relative clause keeps both elements of the Hebrew (מִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה and אֲשֶׁר כָּתַב) while reading more naturally aloud.

text: All Israel—foreigners and native-born alike—with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded, so that the people of Israel would be blessed first.

versions.text: All Israel—foreigners and native-born alike—with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel.
versions.explanation: In the Hebrew, בָּרִאשֹׁנָה ("first") most naturally modifies the act of blessing—the blessing was pronounced before the curse (see v. 34)—rather than the timing of Moses' command. Rendering it as "had commanded earlier" shifts the sense and loses the connection to the following verse's order of blessing and curse.

text: Afterward Joshua read aloud all the words of the law—the blessing and the curse—just as it is written in the Book of the Law.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded which Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who traveled among them.

versions.text: There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded which Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the children, and the foreigners living among them.
versions.explanation: הַטַּף refers specifically to little children/dependents, and הַהֹלֵךְ בְּקִרְבָּם pictures the foreigner journeying along with the community rather than merely residing; the sharper wording preserves the imagery and reads well aloud.
